children.heading: What a social is actually like.

steps.title: You arrive
steps.text: Happy Dog, 5801 Detroit Avenue in Gordon Square. Parking is free. Look for the table with the laptops and the name tags.

steps.title: You grab a dog
steps.text: Fifty-odd toppings, your call. Food and drinks are on you; nothing else costs a thing.

steps.title: You talk
steps.text: No slides. Someone asks what you're curious about, and that is the evening. Beginners and people who build this for a living share a table.

steps.title: The hour after
steps.text: The part people come back for: the introductions, the “you should talk to…”, the project that could use a hand.

steps.title: You head home
steps.text: Three new names in your phone and a reason to come back next month.

children.text: CLE AI & DATA makes AI and data accessible to everyone in Northeast Ohio. As a volunteer-run 501(c)(3) nonprofit, we bring together the people building these technologies and the people learning to use them, through free talks, workshops, socials and community events, so that Cleveland's AI and data jobs are filled by Cleveland people.
CLE AI & DATA (legal name Cleveland AI and Data) is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit, run entirely by volunteers. EIN 42-2843242. Donations are tax-deductible as allowed by law.

In 2010 Doug Meil started a Hadoop user group. Cleveland AI formed in 2017, and in November 2024 the two merged to form CLE AI & DATA. In 2026 we became a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and in November Data in the Land, a community for Northeast Ohio's analysts, data scientists and data engineers, joined us too. Each time, the room got bigger and the conversations got better.

milestones.title: A nonprofit, officially
milestones.body: We incorporate and become a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Still run by volunteers, still free to attend, and now donations are tax-deductible.

milestones.title: Data in the Land joins
milestones.body: A practitioner community focused on skills and careers folds in, bringing weekly job postings and east side meetups.

children.text: . Read it before you come; it's short.
Questions, press, sponsorship, or a code of conduct report:

CLE AI & DATA is for everyone, from the curious to the decision makers. This code applies at everything we run or co-host: talks, socials, workshops, hikes and volunteer days. It also applies in our online spaces: Discord, Meetup, our Substack and social media. It covers everyone there, including attendees, speakers, sponsors, volunteers and organizers.
Say hello, bring the person at the edge of the circle into the conversation, and assume good intent.
Every question is a fair question here. Explain without talking down, and remember everyone in the room started somewhere.
If someone ends a conversation, declines a follow-up or steps back, let them.
Ask before you photograph, record or quote someone.
Our photographers will ask too. You can always say you'd rather not be in pictures.
Talk about your work and what your company does, but don't pitch people who didn't ask, and don't collect contacts for sales lists. This includes sponsors.
If something seems off, check in with the person, or tell an organizer.

Harassment, intimidation or discrimination of any kind, including about gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, nationality, age, religion, or how much experience someone has.
Unwelcome sexual attention or physical contact, and sexual language or imagery in talks, slides or chat.
Insulting or demeaning comments, in person or online, including ones passed off as jokes.
Following, stalking or deliberately intimidating someone, at an event or afterwards.
Sharing someone's personal information, photos or recordings without their consent.
Using AI to make images, audio, video or text of a real person without their consent, or putting other people's private data into a demo.
Repeatedly disrupting a talk, workshop or conversation.
Getting back at anyone for reporting a concern or helping with a report.
Some of our evenings are at a bar. Drinking is never an excuse for any of the above.
tell any organizer. You'll find us at the welcome table, and we'll step somewhere quiet with you.
, or message an organizer on Discord.
If you or someone else is in danger,
You don't have to be sure something "counts" to tell us, and you can stay anonymous. We'll still act, though we may not be able to follow up with you.
We keep reports confidential and share only what we must to keep people safe. We aim to reply within two days.

Organizers will listen, ask what would help, and decide what to do. That can be a conversation, a warning, asking someone to leave an event, removing them from Discord or Meetup, or banning them from future events. The same goes for speakers and sponsors: we can stop a talk or end a sponsorship. Where we can, we'll let the person who raised the concern know it has been handled.

children.text: Who we are and what this covers

Cleveland AI and Data ("CLE AI & DATA," "we," "us") is an Ohio nonprofit corporation and a 501(c)(3) public charity. We run free talks, workshops, socials and an annual Mega Meetup, and we publish a website at cle-ai.com.

This policy explains what information we collect when you visit our website, join our community, register for or attend an event, or support us, and what we do with it. It also explains how we handle photos, video and recordings at events, since we often record and publish them.

It does not cover the platforms themselves. Meetup, Discord, Eventbrite, Givebutter, YouTube and similar services have their own privacy policies, and what you share there is governed by those.
We collect only what we need to run events, keep in touch and report to the funders who keep our programs free. Most of it you give us directly.

children.text: We keep information in password-protected accounts with two-factor authentication where available, limit access to the volunteers who need it, and use established providers rather than our own servers for payments and email. No method is perfectly secure. If we learn of a breach that affects your personal information, we'll notify you as Ohio law requires.

Our events are designed for adults. People under 18 are welcome at most events with a parent or guardian, but we don't knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 13, and we don't publish identifiable photos of minors without a parent's written permission. and we'll delete it. Youth-specific programs, if we run them, will have their own registration and consent forms.

We'll update this policy when our practices change. The date at the top is the current version. For a significant change, such as a new category of information or a new way we publish recordings, we'll say so in the newsletter and on the website before it takes effect.

name: Curtis O'Neal
bio: Curtis O’Neal is an AI solutions architect and data scientist on the CLE AI & DATA team. His career spans research, enterprise software, data engineering and technical leadership. He explores generative AI, agents and AI-assisted learning with hands-on curiosity and healthy skepticism, and holds an MBA from Case Western Reserve’s Weatherhead School.

name: Helen Shere
bio: Helen Shere is Head of Mentorship and Education at CLE AI & DATA and co-founder of Data in the Land, a Cleveland community for data professionals. A Market Analyst at Cleveland Clinic and former science teacher, she brings years of curriculum design and data experience to building CLE AI & DATA’s mentorship program.

name: Julie Novic
bio: Julie Novic is on the CLE AI & DATA leadership team. She is an AI transformation strategist, AI governance professional and data scientist who draws on her PhD in anthropology to design, develop and implement responsible, human-centric AI solutions.

name: Nicole McCaffrey
bio: Nicole McCaffrey is Head of Marketing and Strategy at CLE AI & DATA. She has 25 years in marketing and strategy, including leading marketing at the Responsible AI Institute and SkillSpout and serving as COO of Cleveland AI firm Pandata. She was Vice Chair of the RITE Board, the Greater Cleveland Partnership’s IT workforce collaborative.

name: Ted Troxell
bio: Ted Troxell is President of CLE AI & DATA, Northeast Ohio’s 4,284-member AI and data community, and a Principal Scientist on the founding technical team at Atomic Industries, where he builds machine-learning systems for manufacturing. He has spent 13 years turning AI research into products, as an engineer, startup CTO and CEO.

name: Tim Nash
bio: Tim Nash is Community Liaison and Substack Editor at CLE AI & DATA. He is building a career in healthcare cybersecurity, protecting patient information, while studying at Valencia College. He served with AmeriCorps NCCC FEMA Corps, helping survivors of natural disasters. An Eagle Scout raised in Shaker Heights, he volunteers monthly at a Cleveland men’s shelter.

name: Will Tatz
bio: Will Tatz is Chief Operating Officer of CLE AI & DATA. A community builder and AI ambassador, he brings more than 20 years in operations, project management, strategy and analytics to bringing people together, exploring new technology and turning ideas into action. He is focused on responsible AI and on making AI accessible to everyone.
